What are some good ways you have made extra money on top of your normal job?
A hobby that also produces something worth selling. Carpentry comes to mind first. Well done hand made pieces can sell for a pretty fair markup as well as save you some cash on furnishing your home.
What Faiz said if you ask me, things like metalworking or crafting really go a long way to bringing some happiness and a little bit of extra cash in to your life.
I have a love for sports so in my spare time I officiate lacrosse. It's in the evenings, I get exercise and make a little extra cash.
Sell your old things on ebay! For me, I have boxes of old video games and consoles(nes,n64,atari,etc) and will steadily sell those for a fair price and use the income to buy new games and such.
I heard some websites like listverse pay for submitted content. But it seems you need a very original idea as so much has already been covered.

This subverse is for people who love DJing and are interested in pushing their craft forward. Feel free to introduce yourself if you share similar feelings. You can start by saying a thing or two about yourself, or responding to the question below:

What makes a DJ great (when all DJs are equally popular)? Would it be technical skills? Song selection? 'Soft' crowd skills? Preparation? Systems and workflow? Innovation? Production sense and skills? And/or something else?

The main point of this subverse is to figure out how different people DJ and to share that collective knowledge.

Lastly, I invite users and mods from /r/beatmatch to come and share original and relevant content on this subverse. Your discussions are highly relevant to this subverse and I'd be more than happy to work with you guys to build this community up. One goal of this subverse is to keep general DJ fluff to a minimum, and to provide only highly useful information for aspiring DJs of any level. From my brief visits to your subreddit, I'd say you guys are doing a good job of that. Each time I log onto your subreddit, I find some new and useful information that can be used to change how I DJ.

That's what I hope /v/DJing will come to accomplish.

Cheers!
